# The Silent Chorus: Telepathic Bond

To the observer, the casting of a *Telepathic Bond* is a subtle affair: translucent filaments of argent light—thin as spider-silk—bridge the brows of the participants, shimmering briefly before fading into the ethereal. Yet, for the caster, the sensation is profound. Shaping the Weave for this rite feels like plucking a bowstring of pure thought. It is a cool, humming resonance in the mind, akin to the vibration of a silver tuning fork held against the skull. One must weave these mental threads with the delicacy of a master seamster; a clumsy hand risks only psychic static.

Legend attributes the spell’s refinement to the Archmage Rary during the Siege of the Iron Pass. Trapped behind enemy lines where a single whisper meant death, Rary allegedly wove his scouts’ collective desperation into a silent, unified lattice. In that moment of shared peril, five minds became a single, lethal organism. Today, it remains the quintessence of tactical coordination—a bridge of velvet thought across the cacophony of war.
